title: NntpQueue .env write is not atomic — crash drops injection source but not message
description: In NntpQueue::enqueue (queue.rs lines 156-161), .msg is written via tmp+rename (atomic), but the .env sidecar is written directly with tokio::fs::write() (not atomic). A crash between the .msg rename and the .env write leaves a .msg with no .env. The drain reads .msg files, finds no .env, and defaults injection_source to SmtpSieve — the article IS delivered (not lost) but with wrong injection attribution. In the current code this means articles that were NntpPost-sourced are misclassified, potentially bypassing drain-user gate checks in the reader. Fix: write .env to a .env.tmp file and rename atomically, consistent with the .msg write and with SmtpRelayQueue's pattern.
